explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/659: is there a set of n points in the plane in which every 4 points determine at least 3 distances, yet the total number of distinct distances is ≪ n/√(log n)? The page records the positive answer (Moree–Osburn lattice construction plus Grayzel's exclusion of the pentagon configuration). The statement asks for a family A n of n-point sets in which every 4-subset has ≥ 3 distinct distances and distinctDistances (A n) = O(n/√(log n)) at atTop. Asking for a whole family is the right reading of '≪' in n. Faithful.
